statement: Within Bourgade's two-dimensional random band matrix hypothesis class, there exists a centered, independent-up-to-symmetry, row-normalized, uniformly subgaussian fixed-W Rademacher ensemble for which no interval-length Wegner bound E Tr 1_I(H) <= C_{N,W}|I||Lambda| holds for all intervals I, even with finite C_{N,W} depending on the fixed finite volume.
assumptions: N>2W, periodic L1 band, all allowed entries have magnitude q_W^{-1/2} and independent fair signs up to symmetry; q_W is the row degree including diagonal.
source: Bourgade arXiv:1807.03031 (0.1), section 2.2 for model class; direct finite-support argument in ATTEMPT.md
proof: Tr H^2=|Lambda| for every configuration, hence some eigenvalue E0 lies in [-1,1]. Choose a fixed configuration H0 (probability 2^{-m}>0). Every interval around its E0 has expected count at least 2^{-m}, which contradicts any linear-in-|I| bound as |I| goes to zero.
remaining_gap: Independent audit pending. This only obstructs a specific Wegner-based proof method; it proves nothing about bulk localization itself.
